name: domain:issue-triage
description: Developer tools: Label new issues as bug, feature request or question. Questions verbatim from cookbooks/issue-triage/spec.json (measured wording). compose returns true unless Jev picked `none`; the label is the choice itself, gated by the confidence cut in rule.frozen.json. Measured weakness: issues maintainers label "question" (48% on test).

artifact.type: one GitHub issue (title and body, truncated)

modules.name: issue-type
modules.purpose: Is this GitHub issue a bug report, a feature request or a question, or not an issue at all?

issueType.instructions: What kind of GitHub issue is this?

criteria.bug: A defect report: the software does something wrong, gives an error, or crashes, compared with what it should do.
criteria.feature: A request for new behaviour, a new option, or a change to existing behaviour that currently works as designed.
criteria.question: The author asks how to do something, or asks for help or clarification, without reporting a defect or requesting a change.
criteria.none: None of these: not an issue about the software (spam, an empty or placeholder text, a test post), or unreadable.

issueType.note: The decision (labelled): bug / feature / question, plus `none` (not an issue, empty, unreadable), the escape option.

hasErrorOutput.instructions: Does the issue include an error message, exception, stack trace or log output produced by the software?

criteria.true: Some error text, exception, traceback or log lines from the software are quoted or pasted in the issue.
criteria.false: No error text or log output from the software appears in the issue.

hasErrorOutput.note: true → bug. Error text, a traceback or log output is present.

hasReproSteps.instructions: Does the issue say what the author did (steps, commands or code they ran) to make the described behaviour happen?
hasReproSteps.note: true → bug. Says what they ran or did.

asksHowTo.instructions: Does the author ask how to do something, or ask whether something is possible?
asksHowTo.note: true → question. Asks how to do something, or whether it is possible.

proposesNew.instructions: Does the author ask for a new option, new behaviour, or a change to how the software currently works?
proposesNew.note: true → feature. Asks for a new option, behaviour or change.

notForJev.judgement: Has a code block / a stack trace
notForJev.instead: A regex on the fence or on "Traceback", "Exception:". Free and exact.
Read the field. It is metadata, and it leaks the label.
Search or embeddings over the tracker; Jev sees one issue.
